newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end weaker, seen range-bound.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end weaker, seen range-bound.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed softer in thin turnover on fears over the impact of a drought and the dollar's strength on fourth quarter earnings, said traders.
The bolsa is seen opening stable with volume remaining light, they said.
"There is no structural reason for the bolsa to change. We will keep seeing sideways movement," said one trader.
The 40-share IPSA index ended down 0.1 percent at 95.66 points. The general IGPA index lost 0.18 percent at 5,201.74 points. Trade was light with turnover of 7.3 billion pesos.
The recent rise in the dollar against the Chilean peso will also hurt non-operating earnings as the company has high levels of dollar-denominated debt, they said.
Endesa ended off 1.02 percent at 243-1/2 pesos. Its American Depositary Receipts slipped 1.43 percent to 17-1/4.
Thermal generator Chilgener rose on news UBS Securities had started coverage of the company with a buy recommendation, said traders.
Traders said the market was undercut by selling by foreign investors who are switching funds to other markets in the region including Brazil which offer higher growth potential.
"Chile is less attractive than other countries in the region. Risks are low, but so are returns," said on dealer.

Hydro-electric generator Endesa fell on concerns that the company is having to buy high-cost power from thermal generators as water levels in its dams are too low to supply all its own needs, said traders.
Chilgener ended up 1.33 percent at 2,280 pesos.
Nortegrande, an investment company associated with fertilizer maker Soquimich climbed on news that the firm's board agreed to a dividend of around one peso a share.
Nortegrande ended up 6.03 percent at 7.7 pesos.
